title.narrative: Improving resilience and wellbeing of vulnerable children in the South through Education activities with integrated Protection and WASH initiatives.

description.narrative: ltpgtSave the Children International (SCI) in collaboration with local partners ISWA and Nabaa, will be implementing an intervention addressing the complex challenges faced by vulnerable children. With a focus on education, child protection, and WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), the project responds to the significant disruptions in Lebanon's education system caused by various crises.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe initiative aims to reach 3086 school-aged children, particularly those affected by economic hardships, displacement, and other vulnerabilities. It aligns with the 2023 Lebanon Crisis Response Plan (LCRP), emphasizing access to quality education, psychosocial support, and protective measures. The project spans multiple regions, including Saida and Ein el Helwe, addressing the urgent needs of communities affected by ongoing conflicts and crises. ltbrgtKey components of the intervention include:lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgt1. Education Programming: The project expands access to quality Non-Formal Education (NFE) for Out-of-School Children (OoSC) , Retention Support (RS) for children enrolled in school but at risk of drop-out, and caregiver engagement for parents and families. Additionally, as part of SCI's Education in Emergencies (EiE) programming, the project also addresses the needs of internally displaced children through remote modalities, offering outreach, social and emotional learning activities, and activities to support learning continuity and catch-up.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgt2. Child Protection (CP): The initiative enhances the protective environment for vulnerable children, focusing on those at risk of child labor, child marriage, and exploitation. It adheres to Child Protection Minimum Standards, offering mental health, psychosocial, and protection support. Specialized case management and referrals to various services are integral to the holistic approach.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgt3. WASH Initiatives: A comprehensive technical assessment of 50 public schools in 2023 identified significant challenges, including disabilities in students, water quality issues, and structural problems. The project aims to address these challenges, ensuring a safe and healthy environment for students.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project targets vulnerable children in need of education support. Program participants include Syrian refugees aged 3-5 and 8-14 who will be reached via the provision of non-formal education (NFE) - specifically, Community-Based Early Childhood Education (CB-ECE) for Syrian children aged 3-5 and Basic Literacy and Numeracy (BLN) for Syrian children aged 8-14. Retention Support (RS) will be delivered to children who are enrolled in formal education (including first and second shift in Lebanese public schools or UNRWA schools) but at risk of dropping out due to low levels of academic achievement. RS targets 40% Lebanese students and 60% refugee students (30% Syrian and 30% Palestinians from Syria or Lebanon). Remote Education in Emergencies (EiE) activities will be delivered to internally displaced children based on current data, the majority of displaced children are Lebanese, but Syrian or Palestinian children can be included in the activities based on need. We are estimating 75% Lebanese and 25% Syrian. Education will serve as the entry point for Child Protection services as well.ltbrgtlt/pgt
